key_insight: Interpretable multi-gene expression programs can predict which lupus nephritis patients respond to specific therapies, with strong performance for MMF and azathioprine but weak performance for hydroxychloroquine and standard care.
clinical_relevance: These response biomarkers could support pre-enrollment patient selection for trials and treatment enrichment, helping avoid enrolling patients unlikely to benefit from a given regimen.
method: Reconstructed a 319-sample lupus nephritis gene-expression cohort spanning four treatment regimens.
Built compact, interpretable multi-gene response programs separately for each regimen.
Compared responder vs non-responder prediction and checked pathway-level consistency across treatments.
evidence_signal: Using 21,914 genes, the best programs reached patient-level AUROC 0.847 for MMF and 0.866 for AZA, while HC and SOC were lower at 0.718 and 0.623, respectively.
watch_item: The study is retrospective and based on one reconstructed dataset, so the programs need external prospective validation before any real-world deployment.
paper_title: Interpretable biomarker programs predict treatment response in lupus nephritis: patient-level validation across four regimens
